scope: Predicate/entity governance for the real-estate vertical only (property status/deadline signals, 10_API/gmv_property_signals.py + gmv_property_claims.py). A separate, domain-neutral + Area35-art ontology registry (GMV_ONTOLOGY_REGISTRY_v0.1.json, same top-level shape: entity_classes[]/predicates[] with status CORE/DOMAIN/CANDIDATE/DEPRECATED and domain[]/range[] typing) exists but only on the unmerged branch worktree-bridge-cse_01EFSz2nNresRvPh9GbfwwzK, 106 commits ahead of its merge-base with main as of 2026-09-28 -- not depended on here deliberately, to avoid pulling in unrelated, unfinished, art-domain-specific work for one real-estate predicate. If that branch is ever merged, CORE-tier entries here (DOCUMENT) should be reconciled against its CORE tier, not treated as permanently separate; entries sharing a class_id/predicate_id with that file (DOCUMENT, CONTRACT) are independent entries with their own real evidence, not assumed identical -- see each entry's own source_reference.
governance_rule: reuse-before-invention, same discipline as the domain-neutral registry this file deliberately does not depend on: a new entity class or predicate must be registered here as CANDIDATE, with real evidence and rationale, before use. It cannot silently enter canonical (CORE/DOMAIN) vocabulary.

status_values.CORE: Domain-neutral, expected to apply across any GMV vertical.
status_values.DOMAIN: Specific to the real-estate vertical. Not expected to generalize without review.
status_values.CANDIDATE: Proposed, evidenced, but not yet governed. May be promoted only by an explicit decision, never silently.
status_values.DEPRECATED: Superseded; retained only so historical references resolve.

note_on_scope_v1: Deliberately minimal, per explicit user decision 2026-09-28: only the deadline signal (validated 14/14 in ~/GMV/models/laya/results/real_estate_validation_summary.md) is registered as a predicate in this version. The risk signal (rischio_alto, validated recall only 2/4) is NOT registered here yet -- it stays a consultative field inside gmv_property_signals.py's own output, not a governed claim, until a reliability-qualifier design is agreed. No BUILDING_ELEMENT/component entity class either -- component context (e.g. 'ascensore', 'crepe strutturali'), where present, stays inline in the claim's evidence_excerpt, not a separate typed entity, per the same explicit decision.
note_on_scope_v2: 2026-09-28, later the same day: user proposed a rich ~110-predicate real-estate vocabulary (documento_*/immobile_*/contratto_*/obbligo_*/rata_*/tributo_*/movimento_*/condominio_*/utenza_*/polizza_*/pratica_*/certificazione_*/valutazione_*/asserzione_*). Not registered wholesale -- Laya cannot populate it (it only answers fixed typed questions, no free-value extraction), and an unvalidated 110-predicate registration would repeat the exact reuse-before-invention violation this file's own governance_rule exists to prevent. Instead: (1) confirmed the real local-extraction mechanism already exists and works for this -- gmv_evidence_pipeline.ollama_extract()/semantic_extract_batch(), already in production for Area35, unmodified, pointed at real-estate documents; (2) a genuinely authoritative reference now exists to validate against: the 'GMV Real Estate Knowledge Pipeline' Notion workspace (built separately, by ChatGPT, cloud-based, expensive -- not part of this repo), with real per-property registers (Immobili/Obblighi e scadenze/Movimenti e allocazioni/Eventi contratti e pratiche/Agenda scadenze) already populated with verified data for GERMIGNAGA/COURMA/VIG35/C2/VM8/WITT12; (3) the entity/predicate entries below were registered only after being evidenced by one real ollama_extract() run against GERMIGNAGA's real 2026 TARI notice, cross-checked against that Notion page's already-verified figures (total EUR 222.00, two EUR 111.00 rate on 15/09/2026 and 15/12/2026) -- not copied from the user's wishlist unvalidated. TRIBUTO and OBBLIGO are modeled as the same synthetic subject entity for a tax notice specifically (a tax IS its own payment obligation) -- a contract-derived obligation (e.g. rent) would need a real separate OBBLIGO linked to its CONTRACT via obbligo_deriva_da_documento, not tested here. Amount/date ranges are still 'string' (not typed number/date), consistent with mentions_deadline's own choice -- typed MEASURE/EVENT ranges are a future refinement, not made here to keep this addition proportionate to the one real case behind it.

entity_classes.definition: A source artifact (contract, verbale, email, report) anchoring provenance. Same concept as gmv_evidence_pipeline.py's file_id (sha256:<hex>) -- this entry names the concept for the registry, it does not introduce a second identity mechanism.

A real-estate property (a building or unit) as a graph-vocabulary subject for claims. NOT a Core OID type -- ADR_DB008_OID_PREFIX_TYPE_CONSISTENCY.md's OID contract is a closed six-prefix map (COR/PER/PLG/RES/SRV/SYS) and this registration does not extend it or claim to. Identity source is Dropbox 02_IMMOBILI/01_PORTFOLIO/<PROPERTY>/OBJECT.yaml (gmv_id, name, aliases). As of 2026-09-28 (realigned same day to match the authoritative 'Codice immobile' convention already used by the GMV Real Estate Knowledge Pipeline Notion workspace, e.g. gmv_id='GERMIGNAGA' not an invented numbering): 3 of 6 real portfolio properties have this file (GERMIGNAGA, COURMA, VIG35); C2/VM8/WITT12 still fall back to their folder name (which already matches the real Codice immobile convention for at least WITT12, confirmed against Notion).
entity_classes.source_reference: ~/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/GMV_MASTER_SYSTEM/02_IMMOBILI/01_PORTFOLIO/ (6 real property folders, checked 2026-09-28); Notion 'Immobili' data sources under each property's Pilota/Scheda page (Codice immobile field, queried live 2026-09-28)

Distinct from OBBLIGO in the user's full proposed vocabulary, but modeled here as the same synthetic subject entity for a tax notice specifically -- see note_on_scope_v2.

entity_classes.definition: A payment obligation deriving from a document (tax notice, contract, invoice). For a TRIBUTO specifically, modeled as the same subject entity as the tax itself (see note_on_scope_v2) -- a contract-derived obligation would be a separate, not-yet-tested case.
entity_classes.source_reference: Same real TARI notice as TRIBUTO above

entity_classes.definition: One installment of an OBBLIGO, with its own amount and due date. Real evidence: the TARI notice's 'IL PAGAMENTO POTRA' ESSERE EFFETTUATO IN DUE RATE: 1^ RATA - 15.09.2026, 2^ RATA - 15.12.2026', EUR 111.00 each (half of the EUR 222.00 total), both already verified in the GERMIGNAGA Notion page.
entity_classes.source_reference: Same real TARI notice as TRIBUTO above

entity_classes.definition: A person or institution acting as debtor, creditor, or other party to an OBBLIGO/TRIBUTO/CONTRACT. Deliberately not split into PERSON vs ORGANIZATION (unlike the unmerged art-domain registry's finer entity granularity) -- not evidenced as a real distinction needed yet on real-estate documents; kept as a single class until a real case demonstrates the split matters.
entity_classes.source_reference: Same real TARI notice as TRIBUTO above -- debtor 'VALERIO GIACOMO MARCO' (a person), creditor 'Comune di Germignaga' (an institution), both real

predicates.definition: Subject document/property text contains an explicit operative deadline (absolute or relative). object_raw is deliberately a STRING (the evidence excerpt itself, e.g. 'entro la fine del mese'), NOT a parsed date -- gmv_property_laya_worker.py's scadenza_presente signal only detects presence, it does not extract or normalize a date value. A future 'expires_on'-style predicate with a real date range is a separate, unvalidated next step, not implied by this one. Range is 'string' rather than a closed vocabulary because the evidence text varies freely (real corpus: 'entro il 20 novembre', 'entro 15 giorni', 'entro la fine del mese').
predicates.source_reference: ~/GMV/models/laya/results/real_estate_validation_summary.md §2 (scadenza_presente combined rule, 14/14 on the real-estate suite, including a negative-evidence past-date case and a genuinely ambiguous case both correctly False)
